data.hypothesis: The measured 128-thread float2 mapping is the strongest prior T3 result (0.2882 ms), while the tested 8-accumulator mapping was slower (0.3389 ms). With the same 1024 CTAs, 256-element tile boundaries, 1024 partials, and 256-thread finalizer, assign each 128-thread CTA's lanes to the first and second tile halves using two scalar streams. This tests whether split coalesced loads can compete with contiguous float2 loads without an alignment-specific path; the controller must measure full-call time and validate all required inputs and the FP64 error bound.
data.notes: Only src/candidate.cu is proposed. No commands or local correctness/performance checks were run; official validation and full-call timing remain for the controller.
transformations: Fuse absolute-value accumulation into the partial-sum kernel, followed by the existing finalizer.
Keep 1024 partial CTAs, 256 input elements per CTA tile, grid-stride tile progression, 1024 partial outputs, and the 256-thread finalizer fixed.
Use 128 threads per partial CTA; each lane accumulates scalar values at offsets threadIdx.x and threadIdx.x + 128 within each tile.
Guard each load against the input count so partial tiles and all tails are handled without assuming input-base vector alignment.
Write every partial and overwrite the output on each call.
